memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now the gates of Jericho were securely barred because of the Israelites. No one went out and no one came in. — Josh 6:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jericho was locked up tight. The gates were barred, no one going out and no one coming in. The city had heard about Israel's God and was gripped with fear, so they did the only thing they knew to do: they shut themselves in behind their walls. From a human point of view, Jericho looked utterly impossible to conquer. A walled city, sealed shut, ready for a long siege.

This single verse sets the scene for one of the greatest miracles in Scripture. And it teaches us something before the story even unfolds: God often does His greatest work where the situation looks most closed and hopeless. The very thing that seemed to guarantee defeat — those thick, barred walls — would become the stage for God's power.

Are you facing a "Jericho" right now? Something that seems shut tight, immovable, impossible? A door that will not open, a wall that will not budge? Take heart. The bigger the wall, the greater the glory when God brings it down.

Notice too that Jericho barred its gates "because of the Israelites" — really, because of Israel's God. Fear had already gripped the city. What looked like impregnable strength was actually a place trembling before the living God. Our impossible situations are never impossible to the Lord. In Christ we are reminded that "what is impossible with man is possible with God" (Luke 18:27). The sealed city was about to be opened by the hand of God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "Jericho" in your life looks completely shut and impossible right now?
2. Do you believe God can work precisely where things seem most hopeless?
3. How does it encourage you that the biggest walls make room for the greatest glory?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, the walls before me look impossible, but nothing is impossible for You. Help me trust You to work where every door seems shut. Amen.
